svg.title: Exposure sets the ceiling. Evidence earns the climb. Guardrails do both jobs.
svg.desc: A chart with authority on the vertical axis — in the loop at the bottom, on the loop in the middle, out of the loop at the top — and exposure rising left to right across four bands. A descending staircase marks the ceiling that exposure sets on authority. Everything below the staircase is permitted, and that is where required controls sit. Inside one band an arrow rises to show a handover promoted on measured evidence. In another band a marker sits above the ceiling, reached by a compensating control, with the note that authority there is carried by an approved template rather than by the agent.
svg.text: Exposure sets the ceiling. Evidence earns the climb.

g.text: undone at a cost, one customer

svg.text: EXPOSURE — HOW HARD TO UNDO, AND WHO IS EXPOSED →

g.text: Everything under the staircase. The controls
required here are read off the profile, not chosen.
Guardrails as required controls. Meet them, hold
the evidence, and the handover climbs one level.
Guardrails that carry the authority themselves.

svg.text: Reversibility R1–R4 and reach H1–H5 as defined in the Agent Authority Model. Handovers shown are illustrative.
